reason: The blanks likely need firing to make a solid floor for the liner.
expectation: The solar heating bay will fire the blanks into stronger floor material, though further preparation may be needed.

alternatives.reason: The felt and fabric might provide cushioning, but the floor material seems like a useful first step.

effect: The fired blocks can provide non-pressure paving for the growing bay.
reaction: The distinction between paving and pressure containment is reassuringly clear.
reason: Place the ceramic blocks in the cleared bay to build the liner's floor.
expectation: The blocks will form a paved base, possibly requiring another protective layer before the liner goes down.

alternatives.reason: Felt and fabric may also protect the liner, but the paving seems useful first.

effect: The level paving removes hollows beneath the pressure liner; the felt and fabric are the only available combination.
reaction: Adjusting the blocks so none rocks makes the floor preparation feel physically sensible.
reason: Combine the felt and fabric, likely to make a protective layer for the liner.
expectation: I expect a padded or insulated covering, though its exact use is uncertain.

effect: The felt and fabric form an underlay that protects the pressure skin from ceramic edges.
reaction: The protective layer has a clear physical purpose.
reason: Place the underlay on the level floor; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: The padded floor should be ready for the pressure envelope, though further preparation may be needed.

effect: The protected floor is complete, and the next goal is an inhabited, illuminated room.
reaction: The load-bearing blocks and protective underlay have distinct, sensible roles.
reason: Place the pressure envelope on the prepared floor; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: The envelope will be installed on the floor, though it may still need air and lighting.

effect: The enclosure is sealed, with its airlock and service spine attached; it still needs breathing gas and lighting.
reaction: The distinction between imported seals and local supporting blocks is clear.
reason: Supply breathing gas to the sealed room; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: The room will become breathable, though the grow lights may still need installation.

effect: The growing room is pressurized and has passed its leak check; it still needs lighting.
reaction: Seeing the envelope lift and become a walkable room is satisfying.
reason: Install the grow-light rails to illuminate the room; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: The rails will provide lighting for the growing room, though they may need a power connection.

effect: The room is illuminated, heated and ventilated, and both chapter goals are complete. The result explains the station connection and the array's capacity.
reaction: The lit room feels like a satisfying payoff to the careful preparation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Pressurizing the enclosure was the strongest moment: the envelope lifting into a walkable room made the construction tangible, and the leak check grounded it physically.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate underlay placement felt somewhat repetitive after making the pad, even though its protective purpose was clear.

surprise.text: I appreciated the explicit distinction between fired blocks carrying weight and imported seals containing pressure; it clarified what local materials could actually do.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although most choices after the first were the only offered combination, leaving little room for decisions.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see the growing room put to use; the construction was physically understandable and its completion gave a tangible payoff, despite the linear choices.
